source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati CIN2 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity and 143,778 square feet of technical space, making it one of only nine Ohio facilities with a disclosed megawatt figure.

The disclosed number is the input, not the answer. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density for CIN2, so any conversion to racks is an assumption. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 11 MW is roughly 275 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 1,100. The same 11 MW supports very different amounts of compute depending on a figure CyrusOne does not provide.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, qualify the campus for regulated workloads rather than AI workloads specifically. They say what data the building is permitted to hold, not who holds it. No tenant names are published, so the certifications cannot be read as evidence of AI tenants.

Ohio has 79 mapped facilities and only 9 publish a megawatt figure. Those 9 total 118.4 MW, and CIN2's 11 MW ranks fourth among them. The state total therefore reflects disclosure choices, not installed capacity, and the true Ohio figure is at least as large as what is published and probably much larger. CIN2 is a mid-sized entry in a small disclosed set, and nothing here establishes how much of its load serves AI.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
